domains.label: General Purpose
domains.rationale: The talk is primarily about realtime voice AI systems including TTS, speech-to-speech models, and voice agent pipelines with millisecond-latency requirements. Cartesia's voice AI spans multiple industries with explicit customer support use cases and AWS developer-platform integration via SageMaker Jumpstart and Bedrock. The discussion covers production serving with Sonic 2, edge versus cloud deployment tradeoffs, and evaluation-based monitoring of voice agent systems. The fireside chat is technically grounded but accessible, touching on model architecture and inference latency without deep mathematical derivations. The session is an explicit fireside chat between Cartesia's co-founder and AWS's Rohit Talluri with audience Q&A segments. Eight transcript anchors with said_in_transcript grade directly support the realtime voice AI classification.

summary: Arjun Desai, co-founder of Cartesia AI, presents alongside AWS's Rohit Talluri in a fireside chat about serving voice AI at scale. Cartesia builds real-time multimodal intelligence designed to run on any device, with this session focused on enterprise voice AI. Desai contrasts traditional foundation models—hosted in the cloud, operating in batch mode with 500-600ms response times—with the demands of interactive voice applications where users expect millisecond-level responses. Cartesia approaches voice AI from first principles, focusing on three pillars: quality, latency, and controllability. The company pioneered state space models (SSMs) as an alternative to transformers, achieving O(1) inference-time generation by maintaining a fixed state. Their main product, Sonic 2, is a text-to-speech model serving as one component in a voice agent pipeline alongside an LLM and speech-to-text model, creating latency slack for the LLM. The biggest customer challenge is insufficient latency budget since LLMs are not built for low-latency workflows. Controllability features include voice cloning, accent handling, and native background noise capture. Use cases span healthcare, customer support, real-time gaming, and narration, plus a voice marketplace where voice actors can license their personas. AWS emphasizes optionality through model gardens like SageMaker Jumpstart and Amazon Bedrock, actively seeking new foundation model providers like Cartesia to unlock underserved industries. On data scaling, Desai notes that audio preference data is so diverse that it cannot be captured by a single fine-tuning stage—both rich high-quality data and scale matter. He views speech-to-speech models as immature and not yet production-ready, with orchestrated solutions providing superior controllability. Cartesia's edge models run approximately 5x faster than cloud roundtrips, achieving 40ms model latency—2.5x faster than initial models—while also handling edge cases that LLMs often encounter. For monitoring, Desai emphasizes evaluations as critical, noting issues typically arise at the LLM stage. Looking to 2030, he envisions voice AI as the de facto norm across industries and anticipates real-time interactive world models that go beyond audio to help users understand the world in new ways.

sections.title: Introduction and Voice AI Context
sections.summary: Arjun Desai introduces Cartesia AI, which builds real-time multimodal intelligence for any device. He contrasts traditional cloud-hosted batch foundation models (500-600ms response) with interactive voice applications where millisecond-level latency is critical for user experience.

sections.title: Three Pillars and State Space Models
sections.summary: Desai outlines Cartesia's three priorities—quality, latency, and controllability—and introduces their pioneering state space model architecture. SSMs achieve O(1) inference-time generation by maintaining a fixed state, unlike transformers' quadratic scaling. Cartesia claims to have closed the quality gap with transformers.

sections.title: Customer Challenges and Use Cases
sections.summary: Rohit Talluri transitions to a Q&A format. Desai discusses the main product Sonic 2, the voice agent pipeline (TTS + LLM + STT), and the biggest challenge of insufficient latency budget for LLMs. Use cases include healthcare, customer support, and real-time gaming with dynamic NPCs.

sections.title: Voice Marketplace and Human Narration
sections.summary: Desai discusses Cartesia's voice marketplace for creators, emphasizing the goal of amplifying voice actors rather than replacing them. Voice actors can license their personas on the platform, and narration remains a significant use case.

sections.title: Audience Q&A on End-to-End Latency
sections.summary: An audience member asks about Claude's latency in a Cartesia-Pipecat integration. Desai explains Cartesia's TTS speed creates slack for the LLM but that LLM providers must optimize their own stacks. Talluri highlights AWS's design philosophy of optionality through model gardens like SageMaker Jumpstart and Amazon Bedrock, actively seeking new providers like Cartesia to unlock underserved industries.

sections.title: Voice AI Data Scaling and Speech-to-Speech Models
sections.summary: An audience question about data scaling versus data density in voice AI prompts Desai to explain that audio preference data is so diverse it cannot be captured by a single fine-tuning stage—both rich high-quality data and scale are needed. On speech-to-speech models, Desai considers them immature and not yet production-ready, with orchestrated solutions providing superior controllability. He acknowledges speech-to-speech may dominate over time but requires controllability designed from first principles.

sections.title: Edge Deployment, Monitoring, and Future Vision
sections.summary: Desai discusses Cartesia's edge model capabilities, noting edge deployment is approximately 5x faster than cloud roundtrip with 40ms model latency—2.5x faster than initial models—while also handling edge cases for customers. On monitoring, he emphasizes evaluations as critical and notes issues typically arise at the LLM stage. Looking to 2030, he envisions voice AI as the de facto norm across industries and anticipates real-time interactive world models that help users understand the world in new ways.
